newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin doctor says Yeltsin operation next month.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin doctor says Yeltsin operation next month.

text.p: The Kremlin's top doctor said on Wednesday that Russian President Boris Yeltsin would have heart surgery in mid-November and firmly dismissed speculation that the operation might have to be cancelled.

Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin medical centre, indicated that Yeltsin had had a blood problem at some stage. But he made clear it had cleared up and rallied behind presidential spokesmen by striking an optimistic note.

"The operation on President Boris Yeltsin's heart will be carried out as planned in the middle of November," Mironov told Interfax news agency. "There are no grounds to say that Boris Yeltsin is inoperable."
Kremlin officials on Tuesday had also denied rumours that the operation might be scrapped.

The 65-year-old president pushed ahead with his schedule on Wednesday, meeting President Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow to discuss closer integration with Russia's western neighbour.
Yeltsin dropped out of public view shortly before he was re-elected on July 3 and has handed some of his duties to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

He had two heart attacks last year and one surgeon says he may have had a third this summer. A team of doctors, which will set the date for the operation, has said he is fit enough to withstand surgery but a long preparation period is needed.

Mironov came the closest of any doctors to setting a date for the operation, in which new veins will be grafted in to bypass blocked coronary arteries and improve the supply of blood to Yeltisn's heart.
He made clear that doctors had been worried about "elements of anaemia" -- a shortage of the red blood cells which play a key role in carrying oxygen around the body.
"Now this problem is gradually being solved and there are no blood supply problems which would make the operation impossible," Mironov said.
The treatment Yeltsin was getting had resulted in "positive changes" in the quality of his blood, Mironov said.

Rumours about Yeltsin's health have unsettled financial markets in Russia and the West and the Kremlin has frequently denied them. Even so, Russian share prices again fell on the rumours on Wednesday.
While Yeltsin is in the sanatorium, rivals for power have been squabbling and problems have piled up for the government.

The opposition-dominated State Duma, the lower house of parliament, struck another blow by formally rejecting the government's 1997 budget draft at a first reading and asked ministers to revise the main figures in the draft.
Chernomyrdin had talks with opposition communist leader Gennady Zyuganov on a wide range of social and economic issues.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry arrived on a brief visit to Moscow with a call to the Duma to ratify the START-2 treaty which would cut U.S. and Russian strategic nuclear warheads from 6,000 each to about 3,000 each by the year 2003.
"Reducing the number of weapons you have by half has to be a cost saver," Perry told reporters on his way to Moscow.

The U.S. Senate ratified START-2 earlier this year. Perry said ratifcation by the Duma would save Russia billions of dollars which would otherwise have to be spent on maintaining their strategic nuclear weapons.
Perry was due to address the Duma on Thursday, when he will also hold talks with Chernomyrdin.
